title: Multi-SDK evented invocation patterns for streaming, tools, and typed structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement cross-language SDK patterns to support evented/streaming responses that include tool/function invocation events and typed structured outputs. Deliver runtime-compatible interfaces and examples for TypeScript, Python, and Go that: 1) emit incremental typed JSON payloads (structured output), 2) surface tool invocation and tool result events in-stream, 3) provide backpressure/resumption hooks and compatibility shims for older clients, and 4) document migration guidance for existing SDK users.
acceptance_criteria: TypeScript SDK exposes an EventStream abstraction that yields three event types: delta (text/token), tool_invocation (typed schema), and structured_chunk (typed JSON partials).
Python SDK provides an async generator with the same event envelope and clear examples for consuming and resuming streams.
Go SDK offers a channel-based iterator and a small compatibility shim for clients that expect plain string chunks.

All three SDKs include example snippets showing: invoking a tool via function-call, handling in-stream tool_result events, assembling structured objects from partial JSON chunks, and fallback behavior when structured mode is unavailable.
Compatibility guidelines and migration doc included (Confluence/Drive link).
Automated tests added for: event envelope roundtrip, partial JSON assembly, tool invocation/response ordering, and backpressure signals.
tasks: Define canonical event envelope (type, id, timestamp, payload) and JSON schema for tool_invocation and structured_chunk events.
Implement TypeScript EventStream API and add examples in docs site and quickstart templates.
Implement Python async generator parity and examples for FastAPI/async client use-cases.
Implement Go iterator and provide a small adapter for legacy readers expecting newline-delimited text.
Add unit/integration tests across SDKs that simulate partial JSON emission and out-of-order tool_result arrival.
Write migration guide: mapping old stream callbacks -> new event handlers, and shim code for clients that cannot parse typed events.
Add telemetry hooks to Redwood Console: event counts, missed-JSON errors, tool-invocation latency per client SDK.
Collect feedback from Solutions and Docs teams and iterate on ergonomics.
decisions: Use an explicit top-level 'event_type' field instead of relying on ad-hoc shape detection to make parsers deterministic and simpler to shim across languages.

Structured partials will be emitted as newline-prefixed JSON chunks with a 'structured_chunk' envelope that includes 'path' and 'complete' flags to allow streaming assembly without re-parsing full objects on each chunk.
Tool invocation events will include a reference id that ties the invocation to subsequent tool_result events; SDKs will surface a small helper to correlate these automatically.

Backpressure will be signaled via a numeric 'window' field and optional 'pause'/'resume' control messages in the same event stream; SDKs will expose a soft API to opt into manual or automatic flow control.
notes: Aim for minimal runtime dependency footprint for all SDKs (no heavy JSON streaming libs).
Be mindful of mobile/edge clients that may not parse partial JSON; provide a helper that will assemble and validate when needed.
We need to coordinate with runtime team for a small wire-format change (add 'event_type'). Runtime PR must be ready before SDK shipping.
Consider an optional compact binary envelope in a follow-up for high-throughput customers, but keep initial rollout JSON-first for compatibility.
examples:
Python example:
from redwood import create_event_generator
async for evt in create_event_generator(model='gpt-compatible', structured=True):
    if evt['event_type'] == 'delta':
        print(evt['payload']['text'], end='')
    elif evt['event_type'] == 'tool_invocation':
        # correlate and call tool from server-side helper
        result = await call_tool(evt['payload']['tool_name'], evt['payload']['args'])
        await evt['respond']({'event_type': 'tool_result', 'invocation_id': evt['payload']['invocation_id'], 'result': result})
    elif evt['event_type'] == 'structured_chunk':
        assembler.push(evt['payload'])
# assembler.finish() -> validated dict

Migration note:
Old SDKs used a 'text' callback that emitted tokens. Migration steps:
1) Replace token callback with an iterator/async generator that yields event envelopes.
2) If you cannot parse structured events, use adapter: sdk.stream.toLegacyText() which replays deltas and concatenates structured chunks into text fallback.
3) For tool-calling: map your previous onToolRequest callback to the new tool_invocation handler which receives invocation_id for correlation.
